docs.title: Wire-EDM tactics — multi-pass skim scheduling + recast-layer management
docs.summary: Why multi-pass — the rough/skim split: A wide, slightly tapered/bowed kerf (wire deflects under discharge + flushing force) · Offset scheduling — the geometry: Rough pass: offset leaves stock (e.g. +0.05-0.10 mm of material on the part side) for the skims to remove. · Skim-pass anti-patterns from the floor: "More skim passes = always better." Past the spec requirement, skim passes are wasted cycle time. A part that needs Ra 1.0 μm doesn't need 6 passes; 3 gets there. Match passes to spec. · Tie-ins: [[wedm-tactics-wire-and-flushing]] — sibling WEDM tactical entry (wire + tension + flushing) · Cross-references: [[wedm-tactics-wire-and-flushing]] — sibling WEDM tactical entry

docs.title: WEDM tactics — taper/UV, corner strategy, and FA-10S program structure
docs.summary: Taper / UV cutting: Set ALL H-registers to ZERO on a taper program. The Mastercam Mitsubishi-FA post handles geometric taper compensation in the UV coordinates themselves; a non-zero wire-offset H double-compensates and produces the wrong taper angle. Ground truth: NOZE TEST.NC (E28xx 5-pass UV stainless) runs H175=0 and H1..H5 = 0.0000. *(wedm-jmd-005, jm-die-004, tech-tables E28XX_TAPER_5PASS offset_mm:0)* · Corner strategy: Wire breaks at sharp inside corners (<R0.5 mm) — the wire bends around the corner while discharge energy concentrates on a smaller area. Mitigations: reduce feed to 60% where corner radius < 2× wire dia, increase OFF time 20–30% in corner segments, step down to 0.20 mm

docs.title: Wire-EDM tactics — wire selection, tension, and flushing strategy
docs.summary: Wire tension: Too low → wire bows under flushing pressure + discharge force → barrel-shaped cut, taper error, poor straightness on tall parts. · Anti-patterns from the floor: "Plain brass for everything." Plain brass is the default, not the universal answer. Tall parts (> 100 mm) + high-speed jobs + auto-threading reliability all favor coated/zinc wire. The wire cost delta is small vs the break-recovery cost. · Tie-ins: [[wedm-tactics-multipass-and-recast]] — sibling WEDM tactical entry (skim passes + recast) · Cross-references: [[wedm-tactics-multipass-and-recast]] — sibling WEDM tactical entry

docs.title: Half-wire bug class — action in z.enum + slimmer but no compute() call site
docs.summary: R12 fail-loud relationship: Layer 1 (engine): compute() itself returns a structured object with explicit field names. R12-conformant. · Apply: Before declaring a dispatcher action "wired" in an audit: assert (1) action in z.enum, (2) case statement exists in same dispatcher file, (3) case body invokes engine, (4) if slimmer case exists, slimmer fields exist on engine's return shape.
